newsitem.title: USA: PennCorp. acquires Washington National for $400 million.
newsitem.headline: PennCorp. acquires Washington National for $400 million.

text.p: Life insurance company PennCorp Financial Group Inc. will acquire Illinois-based Washington National Corp. for $400 million, the company said Friday.

PennCorp said it will pay a combination of stock and cash totalling $29.50 a share for Washington National, an insurance holding company with two main operating subsidiaries, Washington National Insurance Co. and United Presidential Life.
Washington National writes disability products to the educator market, and United Presidential writes universal life products.

PennCorp., also an insurance holding company, underwrites and markets life, annuities and fixed benefit accident and sickness insurance to the middle market throughout the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean basin.
"We are excited about adding these two quality insurance operations into PennCorp," said David J. Stone, chairman of PennCorp.

"Washington National Insurance Company and United Presidential provide PennCorp with additional distribution channels into our target middle market, substantial cross-marketing opportunities and the potential for significant consolidation savings.
"Additionally, this transaction evidences PennCorp's continuing plan of consolidating life insurance companies in transactions that make financial sense and which are accretive to earnings."

PennCorp's stock lost $1.75 to $33.375 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange while Washington National, which had been rising on merger expectations, lost $1.375 to $28.50, also on the NYSE.
